newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says up to markets to fix dollar-euro rate.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says up to markets to fix dollar-euro rate.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday that it would be up to financial markets to decide the parity between the future euro single currency and the dollar.
"The right parity is the one which allows us to have the lowest possible interest rates," Arthuis told a conference on the euro currency.
"It is the market which will fix the parity between the dollar and the euro," he said.
"Let's stop these fantasies about parity," Arthuis said.
However, he said he believed the dollar still had room to appreciate.
"I believe that today the dollar has a margin for appreciation," Arthuis said.
He noted he had said this when the dollar was at 5.20 French francs. The dollar is now slightly weaker at 5.09 against the franc.
He also said the dollar exchange rate would be less of a problem when Europe had its single currency. He based that comment on the grounds that more goods would be priced in euros.
